'''Aryeh''' ('''Arie''') '''Dvoretzky''' ({{langx|he| אריה דבורצקי}}, {{langx|ru|Арье Дворецкий}}; May 3, 1916 &ndash; May 8, 2008) was a Ukrainian-born [[Israel]]i [[mathematician]], the winner of the 1973 [[Israel Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref name=prize>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site - Recipients in 1973 (in Hebrew)| url = http://cms.education.gov.il/educationcms/units/prasisrael/tashlag/tashmab_tashlag_rikuz.htm?dictionarykey=tashlag}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3541080,00.html Israel prize winner Prof. Aryeh Dvoretzky dies at 92]</ref> He is best known for his work in [[functional analysis]], [[statistics]] and [[probability]]. He was the eighth president of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].

==Biography==
Aryeh Dvoretzky was born in [[Khorol, Ukraine|Khorol]], [[Russian Empire|Imperial Russia]] (now [[Ukraine]]). His family [[aliyah|immigrated]] to [[Mandatory Palestine|Palestine]] in 1922.<ref>[http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/37/7 Obituary] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090514153415/http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/37/7 |date=May 14, 2009 }}, by Joseph Yahav, Hebrew University of Jerusalem.</ref> He graduated from the [[Hebrew Reali School]] in Haifa in 1933, and received his [[Ph.D.]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1941.  His advisor was [[Michael Fekete]].  He continued working in [[Jerusalem]], becoming a full professor in 1951, the first graduate of the Hebrew University to achieve this distinction.<ref>{{cite journal | title=In memoriam | url=http://www.ma.huji.ac.il/info/001_Dvor1.pdf | journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] | volume=167 | pages=411–412 | date=2008 | doi=10.1007/s11856-008-1053-7 | doi-access=free}}</ref>  
Dvoretzky's son Gideon was killed in the 1973 [[Yom Kippur War]].

==Academic career==
Dvoretzky had visiting appointments at a number of universities, including [[Collège de France]], [[Columbia University]], [[Purdue University]], [[Stanford University]], and the [[University of California, Berkeley]].  He also visited twice the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] (in 1948&ndash;1950 and in 1957&ndash;1958).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/aryeh-dvoretzky|title=Aryeh Dvoretzky|work=Scholars|date=9 December 2019 |publisher=Institute for Advanced Study|access-date=2024-02-21}}</ref>
In 1975, he founded the [[Some Institutes for Advanced Study|Institute for Advanced Studies]] of Jerusalem based on the Princeton IAS model.<ref>[http://www.as.huji.ac.il/mission.php The Institute Mission] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610150207/http://www.as.huji.ac.il/mission.php |date=June 10, 2008 }}</ref> Dvoretzky was the [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the Faculty of Sciences (1955&ndash;1956) and Vice President of the Hebrew University (1959&ndash;1961). He was elected president of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] (1974&ndash;1980) and became the eighth president of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (1986&ndash;1989).  He was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1996.<ref>[http://www.tau.ac.il/honorroll.html Honorary doctor of philosophy (by year)]</ref> Dvoretzky's students included [[Branko Grünbaum]] and [[Joram Lindenstrauss]].

==Business and civic career==
In 1960, he became the head of [[Rafael Advanced Defense Systems Ltd.|Rafael]], the weapons development authority.  He later became the chief scientist for the [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israel Ministry of Defense]].<ref>''1967: Israel, the War, and the Year That Transformed the Middle East'' by [[Tom Segev]] and Jessica Cohen (2007), p. 528.</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
In 1998, received the [[Solomon Bublick Award]] of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. In 1973, he was awarded [[Israel Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref name=prize>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site - Recipients in 1973 (in Hebrew)| url = http://cms.education.gov.il/educationcms/units/prasisrael/tashlag/tashmab_tashlag_rikuz.htm?dictionarykey=tashlag}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3541080,00.html Israel prize winner Prof. Aryeh Dvoretzky dies at 92]</ref>
